steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat the cream cheese with 1 1/2 cups of sugar, and the vanilla extract in a bowl until smooth. Unroll the cans of crescent roll dough, and use a rolling pin to shape the each piece into 9x13 inch rectangles. Press one piece into the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. Evenly spread the cream cheese mixture into the baking dish, then cover with the remaining piece of crescent dough.

Drizzle the melted butter evenly over the top of the cheesecake. Stir the remaining 1/2 cup of sugar together with the cinnamon in a small bowl, and sprinkle over the cheesecake along with the almonds.
Bake in the preheated oven until the crescent dough has puffed and turned golden brown, about 45 minutes. Cool completely in the pan before cutting into 12 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Sopapilla Cheesecake Dessert
raw_recipe.description: Cream cheese, canned crescent rolls, cinnamon, and almonds create this delicious, Mexican-inspired dessert.

review.reviewBody: My rating is for the recipe as is, it's very good. I won't change a recipe then rate it based on the changes. And quite frankley I don't know why allrecipes allows that, it's certainly not fair to the submitter. Having said that, IMHO adding an egg to the cream cheese/sugar mixture turns this into a 5 star recipe!

Just a note there is another listed "Cream Cheese Squares" that is the same w/o the nuts - whichever way you make it - DELICIOUS. (if you want to add a flavor, try raspberry pie filling on top of cheese layer, then the other layer of dough & cinn & sugar; or Lemon Curd/pie filling - heaven!!)
I get requests for this at potlucks. Very good. I cut the butter down a little. I didn't like seeing it sitting in puddles on top when I took it out of the oven.

Yum! I made this recipe as presented but needed individual, easy to serve portions for a potluck so I cut the dough into 4x4 squares and filled them with 1 tablespoon of the cream cheese mixture, pulled the corners together and then pressed them down to form a pouch. I brushed with butter, sprinkled the tops with the cinnamon/sugar and almonds. These only needed to bake for 18 minutes to get golden brown. So pretty and tasty! They were a hit!
Very simple. I followed the recipe except only used 1 Cup sugar as cream cheese is already sweetened. I also added one egg to bind the filling better and make it more stable.

I made this for potluck and it was a big hit. I made this for the first time in a long time and will definitely make it more often since I realized I can make and freeze ahead of time. To freeze, I made per the recipe except in step 3 I only topped with melted butter and baked. After cooling completely I put it in fridge for a couple hours to firm up then removed from pan, wrapped completely with plastic wrap then with foil and froze. When ready to use I removed foil and left in plastic wrap and put in fridge 24 hours to thaw. Then I put back in pan I had baked in, topped with sugar and cinnamon ( I made 1/3 cup sugar and 2 teaspoons sugar but only used about 1/2 of mixture) and put in 350 degree oven for about 12 minutes.

I added 1/2 teaspoon more cinnamon. And layer brown sugar, sugar and cinnamon on bottom pie crust. Also, used organic vanilla, and irish butter which increased richness of flavor. My husband had eaten a cup of filling before it reached the pan. A perfect hit.

Very rich recipe and pretty easy to make. I added an egg to the cream cheese filling per other reviewers and 1/4 c. of honey on top, because, when I first had sopapillas in New Mexico they were served with honey. I will definitely add cherry/apple pie filling on top of the cream cheese next time.

I've made this so many times over the years and it's always a HUGE hit. At one time I used this recipe to make strawberry cheesecake French toast for breakfast. I substituted the cans of crescent rolls with French toast, used the same amount of cream cheese and sugar and vanilla in the filling, but omitted the butter and cinnamon-sugar mix on top since I always fry my French toast. After baking, I topped with strawberry pie filling. Fantastic!

I've made this a couple of times, years apart. When I made it last week, my husband exclaimed that it was the best thing I've ever made. :) I added an egg to the cream cheese mixture as some others have suggested. Prior to adding the cream cheese mixture, I sprinkled sliced almonds and brown sugar over the dough. On top of the cream cheese mixture, I spread a can of apple pie filling sprinkled with extra cinnamon and brown sugar. Next time, I am considering using two cans of the apple pie filling instead. On top, I used a lot more almonds and used a combination of white and brown sugar (1/2 to 1/3 of mixture was brown sugar), using as much cinnamon sugar mixture as seemed appropriate (I just mixed up a dish of it). I used the same amount of butter called for in the recipe. I baked it for 55 minutes, and the majority (especially the middle) of the cream cheese mixture was still very soft. I'd like to have it set up/dry out more like an actual cheesecake. Any pointers (do I need to add a second egg??)? Anyway, it was absolutely delicious. My son and husband went crazy over it. The topping made it crunchy, which was a real plus for us. I plan to make this again for Thanksgiving dinner.

Great! Easy! I did follow some suggestions to substitute 1 cup ricotta because I had two cups I was trying to use up. Also added an egg as someone suggested. I tried to roll dough out, but it stuck and tore. I just put it in the 9x13 pan. (greased) It fits perfectly and the small perforations disappear in baking. I just unrolled the top crescent roll crust onto the cream cheese, ricotta, egg, vanilla mixture. Mixed sugar and cinnamon with finely chopped pecans because that’s what I had in the refrigerator. Baked 45 minutes. Perfect. Even better the next day straight from the fridge!
Can add or subtract any different ways… but love way it is too… yumba!
Cannot wait to bake this I have done a few of these recipes and they ARE LOVED
Super simple recipe that commands a lot of tasty respect! I'll make this again and again.
Made it just like the recipe says.
I have now made them multiple times. Everyone loves them.
Next time I would use less sugar. But everyone loved it. We warmed it just a little 😋

I baked the bottom crust first (like one suggestion). I felt it had too much crust. Needs more lemon flavor. I added 1/4 teaspoon of lemon abstract could have used more. Overall it was good. Will try again.
My family wants this all the time. Easy to make and take anywhere. You never bring any back home.❤️
Love it easy and simple.
